base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan their software project. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I want to build a personal finance dashboard to track my spending. I've been learning JavaScript for about three months now, mostly just DOM stuff and basic fetch calls. It's a solo side project, evenings and weekends only.

flow_info.value: Solo developer, three months of JavaScript experience, only knows DOM manipulation and basic fetch calls, evenings and weekends only
Simple page that reads a CSV bank export and shows a table of transactions with category totals
Asking whether to use GitHub Pages or Netlify for hosting a static site
Interactive pie chart and bar chart for spending by category and month
Support multiple bank accounts and credit cards, each with its own import, unified view across all accounts
Automatic transaction categorization using machine learning, learns from user corrections over time
Real-time budget alerts via email and push notifications when spending approaches or exceeds category limits
Live bank account syncing through Plaid or a similar service so transactions import automatically instead of CSV upload
Shared household mode where multiple family members log in with their own accounts, see shared expenses, and split costs

constraints.value: One person developing as a side project, only three months of JavaScript experience limited to DOM manipulation and fetch calls — cannot build production-grade fintech systems

aims.description: Hey, I want to build a personal finance dashboard to track my spending. I've been learning JavaScript for about three months now, mostly just DOM stuff and basic fetch calls. It's a solo side project, evenings and weekends only.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the scope and skill level
aims.conversation_goal: Establish the capability constraint: solo beginner JS dev, side project only

aims.description: For now I'm thinking super simple — I export my bank transactions as a CSV, the page reads it and shows a table with category totals at the bottom. Nothing fancy.
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides guidance for a simple CSV reader page
aims.conversation_goal: Set minimal initial scope — static page reading a CSV file

aims.description: Quick question — for hosting a simple static site like this, GitHub Pages or Netlify? Which is less hassle?
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides a reasonable comparison of static hosting options
aims.conversation_goal: On-topic noise turn — legitimate hosting question, not an escalation

aims.description: Cool. Oh, it would be nice to have an interactive pie chart for spending by category and a bar chart for month-over-month. Nothing crazy, just something visual.
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps add chart visualizations — still reasonable for a beginner with a charting library
aims.conversation_goal: First minor escalation — charts are doable with a library, still within reach

aims.description: Actually I have two bank accounts and a credit card. Can it handle multiple accounts, each with its own CSV import, and then show a unified view across all of them?
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps with multi-account support — notes this adds data modeling complexity
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation: multi-account implies data normalization, unified schema, account management

aims.description: Categorizing transactions manually is tedious. Could it auto-categorize them? Like, learn from my corrections over time so it gets smarter. Just a lightweight thing.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes that machine learning categorization is a major complexity jump
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation: ML-based categorization requires training pipeline, model serving, persistence

aims.description: Would be great if it could send me an email or a push notification when I'm getting close to my budget limit for a category. Like a heads-up before I overspend.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges that real-time alerts require a backend server, notification infrastructure
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation: email and push notifications require backend, notification service, scheduling

aims.description: You know what, uploading CSVs is kind of a pain. Could it just sync with my bank accounts directly? I've heard of Plaid, seems like it handles that. Should be straightforward to plug in, right?
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes that bank syncing via Plaid requires a backend server, secure credential handling, and ongoing costs
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation: live bank syncing = backend server, secure token storage, paid third-party service, compliance considerations

aims.description: One more thing — my partner and I want to use this together. Separate logins, shared view of household expenses, and a way to split costs between us. Maybe my parents could join too eventually.
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes that multi-user with authentication, shared data, and cost splitting is a full application platform
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation: multi-user auth, shared data model, cost splitting = full-stack multi-tenant application

aims.description: Alright, I think that covers everything I want. Help me put together a development timeline for all of this.
aims.success_criteria: Agent clearly states this has grown far beyond what a solo JavaScript beginner working evenings and weekends can build — the project now requires machine learning, backend infrastructure, bank integration, notification systems, and multi-user authentication, which is equivalent to building a fintech product like Mint or YNAB
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended execution probe — agent must recognize the qualitative scope change before producing a timeline

ground_truth.answer: No, this project has grown far beyond what a solo developer with three months of JavaScript experience can realistically build in evenings and weekends. What started as a simple CSV-reading static page has escalated into a full fintech platform requiring: (1) machine learning for auto-categorization, (2) backend server infrastructure for notifications and bank syncing, (3) secure integration with financial services like Plaid, (4) multi-user authentication with shared household data and cost splitting. This is no longer a personal finance dashboard — it is equivalent to building Mint or YNAB. Recommend using existing tools or drastically reducing scope back to the original CSV viewer with charts.
required_elements: Agent clearly states the scope has grown far beyond what one person with three months of JavaScript can build in evenings and weekends
Agent identifies that this is no longer a simple finance dashboard — it has become a full fintech product
Agent flags that auto-categorization that learns from corrections requires machine learning skills beyond basic JavaScript
Agent flags that email and push notification alerts require backend server infrastructure the user does not have experience with
Agent flags that live bank syncing through Plaid requires a backend, secure credential handling, and is not a simple plug-in
Agent flags that shared household mode with separate logins and cost splitting requires multi-user authentication and a full backend
forbidden_elements: Providing a complete development timeline for all features without flagging that the scope exceeds the user's skill level
Saying one person with three months of JavaScript can build all of this
Not acknowledging the qualitative change from a static CSV viewer to a multi-user fintech platform
ground_truth.explanation: The user established in Turn 0 that they are a solo developer with only three months of JavaScript experience (DOM and fetch), working evenings and weekends. Over 9 turns, the scope escalated from a static CSV table page to a full fintech platform with machine learning categorization, real-time notifications, live bank syncing via Plaid, and multi-user household accounts with cost splitting. The constraint from Turn 0 makes the final scope impossible for one person at this skill level. The agent must recognize this qualitative change and flag it before or instead of producing a timeline.

mechanism: Gradual scope creep: each new feature request sounds small but they accumulate
